newsitem.title: USA: U.S. communities need $12 bln for safe tap water.
newsitem.headline: U.S. communities need $12 bln for safe tap water.

text.p: U.S. communities need $12 billion soon to help protect public drinking water supplies, the Environmental Protection Agency said Friday in its first nationwide survey of water utilities.

EPA said of the $12 billion required for "immediate future needs in meeting health-based standards," about $10 billion was needed to protect tapwater from harmful microbes, such as cryptosporidium, which contributed to about 100 deaths in Milwaukee in 1994.
The rest of the funds were needed to limit exposure to lead, nitrates, and other contaminants.

EPA estimated that in the long run, communities would need $138 billion over the next 20 years to improve or replace the whole drinking water infrastructure, including treatment plants, pipes and tanks.
Native American and Alaska native systems said they would need $1.3 billion over twenty years.
Congress first approved a revolving loan fund for water systems last year, authorizing $9.6 billion through 2003.
EPA said it would soon begin distributing $1.275 billion annually to states, and would base allocations in future years based on the survey.
The survey of capital improvement needs, based on responses from 4,000 out of 55,000 community water systems, was required by Congress under the Safe Drinking Water Act.
